title.narrative: Control and reduction of mercury emissions from the cement industry in Brazil

description.narrative: Health improvements and reduced exposure to hazardous substancesBy reducing mercury emissions from cement kilns and promoting the safe management of input materials and alternative fuels, the project will contribute to improved occupational and public health. Workers in cement plants, waste co-processing facilities, will benefit from lower exposure to mercury and associated health risks, including reproductive, neurological, and respiratory disorders. These improvements are particularly relevant for vulnerable populations such as women of reproductive age, children, and informal sector workers.Creation of sustainable livelihoods and green job opportunitiesThe project will support the growth of sustainable practices in the cement value chain, such as the expanded use of SCMs, improved waste co-processing, and environmental monitoring. These activities will generate demand for new technical roles and services, particularly in environmental analysis, logistics, and sustainable materials sourcing. Targeted capacity building and technical assistance will open up employment opportunities for youth, women, and local service providers, supporting more inclusive green job creation.Strengthening regulatory capacity and institutional resilienceBy improving the regulatory framework for mercury inventory, control and emissions monitoring, the project will enhance Brazil’s institutional capacity to enforce environmental standards and fulfill its Minamata Convention commitments. These institutional improvements will support broader efforts to modernize industrial oversight, increasing transparency and long-term governance resilience across the sector.Market transformation through innovation and competitivenessThrough its focus on clinker substitution, circular material flows, and alternative fuels, the project aligns with global trends in sustainable construction. By helping the industry meet environmental standards, it enhances competitiveness in both domestic and international markets. This transformation will also encourage investment in cleaner technologies and resource-efficient processes, improving the overall productivity and environmental performance of the sector.Improved resource efficiency and circular economy integrationThe project promotes the increased use of industrial by-products (e.g., fly ash, slag, phosphogypsum) as SCMs, diverting waste from landfills and reducing the demand for virgin raw materials. By embedding circular economy principles into cement production, the project contributes to more efficient resource use and reduced environmental degradation.Advancement of gender equity and inclusive participationBy integrating gender-responsive approaches into mercury risk reduction and environmental governance, the project will help address structural inequalities in the cement sector. Women, especially those in administrative, community-facing, or informal roles, will benefit from increased awareness, capacity-building, and representation in decision-making processes. This inclusive approach ensures that environmental benefits are equitably shared and socially sustainable.Support for national environmental and economic prioritiesThe project supports Brazil’s national development goals by aligning industrial decarbonization with chemical safety, circular economy, and inclusive growth. It contributes to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 3 (Good Health and Well-being), 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), and 13 (Climate Action), reinforcing Brazil’s transition to a more sustainable and resilient industrial future.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

To support national commitment towards the Minamata Convention through monitoring, control and reduction of mercury emissions from the cement industry in Brazil and synergies with innovative approaches planned under the Cement Technology Roadmap
